newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
KATHIMERINI

--The pressure on the Cypriot government by the United States and European Union countries is beginning to bear fruit as Ankara begins a provocative air and sea exercise in the Aegean which foresees the cutting off of the islands of Hios and Lesvos from the rest of Greece. Athens, however, insists on defending Nicosia's decision to buy Russian S-300 missiles.
--The government appears to have caved in to pressure from certain sectors with crucial changes to its draft tax legislation bill, presented yesterday.
--Excessive spending on medicines, totalling 2.0 percent of GDP, will be cut back, the government hopes, with the implementation of a new list of medicines covered by health care funds.
--The government's new bill on combatting unemployment hopes to create 30,000 new jobs with subsidies to employers.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--A new wave of strikes is set to hit the country on Monday. Teachers, seamen and, possibly, civil servants will be ready to take to the streets.

--Turkish generals have sent a message to the Turkish foreign ministry that the Aegean is in danger of being lost as Greece is "claiming disputed islands islets without hindrance". A November meeting decided on an attack on Cyprus in the event of a crisis.
--US ambassador to Athens Thomas Niles complains to Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos about Cyprus's missiles purchase. Pangalos defends the decision.
--The European Court will hear three cases against Greece on violation of Community directives on the environment.
--Greece may also be called on to pay a fine for not applying an EU directive on the recognition of academic degrees received abroad.
--A new justice ministry provision will change the procedures to send parliamentary deputies to be tried before special tribunals for abuse of powers.
TA NEA

--The number of medicines subsidised by health funds will be drastically cut back as of March, in an effort to curb overconsumption of medicines, excessive spending on pharmaceuticals and to better control doctors' prescriptions.
--The new economic crimes squad - the 'Rambo' of the tax department - is set to receive powers that will override confidentiality clauses in banking, taxation and other affairs.
--Bulletproof vests are the newest fashion item for robbers, saving one of two robbers who hit a Post Office Savings Bank yesterday.
ETHNOS
--Four Greeks are among the 11 people charged with murder by a Nafplion prosecutor after the sinking of a ship carrying 283 illegal immigrants in the Mediterranean.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS

--The 201 members of the conservative opposition New Democracy party's Central Committee and Parliamentary Group are set today to adopt the agreement worked out between the bickering leadership and leadership contenders earlier this week.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
